note: 2026-10-12 analyst batch, PROPOSED BY THE RESEARCH ANALYST AND COMMITTED ONLY UNDER THE CHAIRMAN'S HAND. THE ONE QUESTION: does ICSID's own case-detail page for ICSID Case No. ARB/24/45 render labelled prose identifying a matter brought by Philippine claimants against the Kingdom of Spain, and what do its 'Subject of Dispute' and 'Instrument(s) Invoked' fields say? The case number ARB/24/45 and the caption 'Nurhima Kiram Fornan and others v. Kingdom of Spain' reached this council ONLY as SEARCH-ENGINE SYNTHESIS PROSE about pages NO SEAT OPENED, and under this council's standing rule that is REFUSED AS A FINDING. NO BODY WAS READ BY ANYONE: WebFetch returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on a neutral control and curl returned CONNECT tunnel failed 403, both probed before anything was spent. This batch exists precisely because the lead cannot be verified any other way: www.italaw.com and bare italaw.com are under this council's standing relay prohibition, so the document itself is unreachable by this instrument and only ICSID's own docket surface is available. WHY THE ROWS ARE WORTH SPENDING: 'Subject of Dispute' is ICSID's own characterisation of the asserted investment and is therefore a PRIMARY-FIELD test of this project's Ring 1 on this matter, where the alternative is the analyst's reading of a Google Scholar snippet; 'Instrument(s) Invoked' is where ICSID names the treaty, against a snippet asserting 'the 1993 Philippines-Spain bilateral investment treaty'. WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS: a holding, a disposition, or any statement about what any tribunal decided. G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition and G10 bars reading a document designation as a tribunal's characterisation. IT ALSO DOES NOT TOUCH THREAD 11: a Rule 41 limb appears ONLY in the refused engine prose, and even if true it could not move thread 11, whose closure requires the stated ground to be whether an IP right is a covered investment - and on the analyst's ruling today this matter asserts no IP at all, so it does not even reach thread 11's third 'gate fired / IP asserted / non-IP ground' bucket. (2) LEXICOGRAPHIC ORDER, which is the defect this project learned on 2026-09-03: newest_request() is sorted(glob('*.json'))[-1] (scripts/fetch_relay.py:newest_request), and '2026-10-12-zz-fornan-arb-24-45.json' sorts above '2026-10-12-daily.json' because 'z' > 'd', so this batch - and not the already-answered daily batch - is what the runner picks up. The designator reached this council only as search-engine synthesis prose about pages no seat opened; that is REFUSED AS A FINDING and stays refused. I approve it anyway because both outcomes are results - a TRUE converts a refused engine caption into a primary-field fact, and a FALSE with its controls green refutes the lead - but no successor may read a TRUE here as vindicating the engine prose this council refused today, which asserted a Rule 41 objection, a hearing date, a claimant count, an arbitrator's criminal sentence and two national-court dates. urls.purpose: SAME-RUN COMPANION CONTROL AND THE RING-1 SUBSTANCE IN ONE ROW. Prior art 31 fired / 31 TRUE on case-detail URLs across 606 rows. Expected TRUE. It establishes that the origin answered and that the tag-strip yielded labelled field prose from THIS byte stream, which is what makes a null on row 3 interpretable at all; a FALSE here VOIDS the reading of row 3's null. It also carries the substance: on every prior firing this field's forward window has carried the adjacent 'Economic Sector', 'Instrument(s) Invoked' and 'Applicable Rules' labels - ARB/18/20 returned 'Subject of Dispute: Renewable energy generation enterprise Economic Sector: Electric Power & Other Energy Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) ECT (Energy Charter Treaty) Applicable Rules: ICSID Convention - Arbitration Rules' (2026-10-12-daily.json idx 4) and ARB/16/34 returned 'Subject of Dispute: Tire and rubber products enterprise Economic Sector: Other Industry Instrument(s) Invoked' (2026-08-25 record). SO THIS ONE ROW IS THE PRIMARY-FIELD TEST OF WHETHER ICSID CHARACTERISES THE ASSERTED INVESTMENT IN THIS MATTER AS ANYTHING IP-RELATED, and of what treaty it names. WHAT IT DOES NOT FOUND: any holding, reasoning or disposition; and nothing about whether the window reaches 'Instrument(s) Invoked' is guaranteed - EXCERPT_CHARS is 400 with a 100-character lookbehind (:42, :134), so a long Subject-of-Dispute string could push the instrument label out of the window, and if it does, that is an instrument observation and not an absence of the field.

SECOND SAME-RUN COMPANION CONTROL, and the procedural posture. Prior art 63 fired / 63 TRUE on case-detail URLs - the strongest-attested find in this project's entire relay corpus. Expected TRUE. WHAT IT FOUNDS: ICSID's own labelled statement of this matter's procedural status as rendered at the batch instant, plus whatever the forward 300 characters carry - on ARB/26/40 that window carried 'Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: October 6, 2026 - The Acting Secretary-General registers a request for the institution of arbitration proceedings' (2026-10-11-daily.json idx 10) and on ARB/18/20 it carried 'Status of Proceeding: Concluded Outcome of Proceeding: September 26, 2025 - The Tribunal renders its award' (2026-10-12-daily.json idx 1). A dated 'Latest Development' or 'Outcome of Proceeding' label here would be ICSID's own dated event prose for this matter. WHAT IT DOES NOT FOUND: the content of any decision, and no disposition - G16. Two controls rather than one because row 3 is a genuine coin-flip and a single control that happened to miss would void the batch's whole reading.

THE IDENTIFICATION ROW, and the only row that tests the lead. NEVER FIRED as a find on this or any host - prior art is zero in both directions and that is stated, not hidden. A TRUE binds the caption to this docket number from ICSID's own prose and converts the engine-sourced caption from refused prose into a primary-field fact about what ICSID renders. A FALSE is interpretable ONLY because rows 1, 2 and 4 are companions on the same URL in the same run, and it would mean one of three things which this row cannot separate: the case number is wrong; ICSID renders a different claimant as the caption; or ICSID renders the name in a form this exact, case-insensitive literal does not match. ROW 4 EXISTS TO SEPARATE THE SECOND AND THIRD FROM THE FIRST. A FALSE IS NEVER A STATEMENT THAT NO SUCH MATTER EXISTS - the project's absence rule is 'not found in accessible sources'.

THE DISAMBIGUATOR for row 3's possible null. Prior art 1 fired / 1 TRUE on case-detail URLs (2026-09-02-daily.json idx 5), and the literal is additionally attested in visible prose inside other finds' windows on this page family - today's ARB/18/20 rows returned 'ant(s)/Nationality(ies): (i) Veolia Propreté SAS (French) Respondent(s): Italian Republic (Italian)' (2026-10-12-daily.json idx 2). Expected TRUE as a label. WHAT IT FOUNDS: ICSID's own rendering of the claimant name or names and their nationalities, WHATEVER STRING ICSID USES - which is what makes a null on row 3 readable as 'ICSID renders this caption differently' rather than as 'the case number is wrong'. Returns the FIRST occurrence in document order only (body.lower().find(), :131), so on a page carrying an original proceeding and a later annulment or revision proceeding it gives up only the first block, and no inference about any later one is authorised. A FALSE is an instrument observation about label rendering on this page and is NEVER a statement about who the claimants are.
